title: Open trial of an internet-based self-help intervention for loneliness
summary:
Loneliness is a widespread and serious health risk associated with negative effects on mental and physical health, increased use of health services, and higher social costs. Loneliness is not necessarily synonymous with social isolation. Even people with many social contacts can feel lonely. Although various measures have been developed to reduce loneliness, there is little evidence of their effectiveness under routine conditions.
The study examines an internet-based self-help intervention (SOLUS) that aims to promote a better understanding of the experience of and coping with feelings of loneliness. The aim is to reduce feelings of loneliness and increase well-being. We are conducting this study to find out whether an evidence-based internet-based self-help program is suitable for reducing feelings of loneliness under routine conditions and to investigate who benefits from it.
